title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 170 (Bailee's particular lien)

content.overview: Section 170 provides that where the bailee has, in accordance with the purpose of the bailment, rendered any service involving the exercise of labour or skill in respect of the goods bailed, he has, in the absence of a contract to the contrary, a right to retain such goods until he receives due remuneration for the services he has rendered in respect of them.
content.glance: Bailee who has rendered services involving labour or skill in accordance with the purpose of the bailment has a particular lien to retain the goods until due remuneration is paid, absent a contrary contract.
content.study: Where the bailee has, in accordance with the purpose of the bailment, rendered any service involving the exercise of labour or skill in respect of the goods bailed, he has, in the absence of a contract to the contrary, a right to retain such goods until he receives due remuneration for the services he has rendered in respect of them. Current-law framing: particular (not general) lien for services involving labour or skill performed for the purpose of the bailment.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: Where the bailee has, in accordance with the purpose of the bailment, rendered any service involving the exercise of labour or skill in respect of the goods bailed, he has, in the absence of a contract to the contrary, a right to retain such goods until he receives due remuneration for the services he has rendered in respect of them.

examples.title: Repairer's lien
examples.body: Bailee repairs goods in accordance with the bailment. Absent contrary contract, he may retain them until due remuneration is paid under Section 170.

hypotheticals.question: Bailee has exercised skill on the goods for the purpose of the bailment. May he retain them until paid?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes, in the absence of a contract to the contrary, under Section 170.

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 170 gives the bailee a right to retain the goods until he receives due remuneration where he has, in accordance with the purpose of the bailment, rendered any service involving the exercise of labour or skill in respect of the goods, in the absence of a contract to the contrary. This is a particular lien limited to the goods and the services rendered on them.
examples: Repairer or skilled worker may retain the goods until paid.
distinctions: Particular lien under Section 170; general lien under Section 171 for specified persons.
